title: Stress and the accent mark
goal: Find the stressed syllable, and know where the accent is written and where it is not.

blocks.text: Stress is part of the word in Greek: it can change meaning (πότε 'when?' vs ποτέ 'never'), and it moves in some forms of nouns and verbs. Every word of two or more syllables carries a written accent (τόνος) on its stressed vowel, so you never have to guess. Learn every word **with its accent**: in this course an unaccented answer is marked 'almost'.

blocks.title: One accent since 1982
blocks.text: Until 1982 Greek was written in the **πολυτονικό** 'polytonic' system, with three accents and two breathing marks inherited from antiquity. The reform introduced the **μονοτονικό**: one accent mark, which simply shows the stress. The Church and some publishers still print polytonic. Stress is the commonest giveaway of a foreign speaker, especially in place names: **Αθήνα** (-θή-), **Θεσσαλονίκη** (-νί-), **Ηράκλειο** (-ρά-), **Χανιά** (-ιά). Some pairs differ only in stress: **Αθήνα** 'Athens' and **Αθηνά** 'the goddess Athena', **γέρος** 'old man' and **γερός** 'sturdy'.

blocks.title: Double accents (enclisis)
blocks.cite: When a weak pronoun follows a word stressed on the third syllable from the end, a second accent is added.

items.prompt: Which of these words is written with an accent?
items.why: One-syllable words take no accent; σπίτι has two syllables.

items.prompt: Which spelling is correct?
items.why: In a vowel pair like οι the accent goes on the second letter.

items.prompt: Which one means 'or'?
items.why: ή 'or' keeps its accent to tell it apart from the article η.

items.prompt: Which is the question word 'where?'
items.why: Question words πού, πώς are accented; που 'that, who' and πως 'that' are not.

items.prompt: How is a capitalised word like 'Όμηρος' accented?
options: Accent on the next vowel: Ομήρος
items.why: An initial capital takes the accent before (above-left of) the letter. Words in all capitals take none: ΟΜΗΡΟΣ.

items.prompt: Πότε and ποτέ differ only in stress. Which means 'never'?
items.why: πότε = when?, ποτέ = never (or ever, in questions).

items.prompt: Which word is stressed on the last syllable?
items.why: καφές carries its accent on the final vowel; the others stress the first or second-to-last syllable.

items.prompt: Genitive singular of **άνθρωπος**: του ___
items.why: Stress can sit no further back than the third-to-last syllable; with a long ending -ου it moves one step right.

items.prompt: **το όνομα** + **μου** 'my name'
items.why: A word stressed on the third-to-last syllable takes a second accent on its last syllable before a weak pronoun.

items.prompt: **ο γιατρός** + **σου** 'your doctor'
items.why: No second accent: γιατρός is stressed on its last syllable, so the pronoun just leans on it.

items.prompt: Which spelling is correct for 'children'?
items.why: The ι of -ιά is a glide, not a syllable, so the accent falls on α.

items.prompt: Which spelling gives three syllables, [ka-í-ki] 'caique'?
items.why: ΐ (diaeresis plus accent) shows that α and ι are separate vowels; καί- would read [ke].

items.prompt: **ΑΘΗΝΑ** on a road sign means the city. In lowercase it is:
items.why: All-capital words drop the accent, but the stress stays: Αθήνα. Αθηνά is the goddess.

items.prompt: 'He is strong' is:
items.why: γερός 'sturdy' is stressed on the end; γέρος means 'old man'.

items.prompt: Ξέρω ___ θα έρθει. 'I know that he will come.'
items.why: The conjunction πως 'that' has no accent; πώς is the question word 'how?'.

items.prompt: Write in lowercase with the accent: **ΚΑΦΕΣ** 'coffee' (stress on the last syllable)
items.why: Multi-syllable words always carry a written accent on the stressed vowel.

items.prompt: Write in lowercase with the accent: **ΘΑΛΑΣΣΑ** 'sea' (stress on the first syllable)
items.why: Third-to-last syllable: θά-λασ-σα.

items.prompt: Write in lowercase with the accent: **ΠΑΙΔΙ** 'child' (stress on the last syllable)
items.why: The accent goes on the stressed vowel ι, not on the digraph αι.

items.prompt: Write in lowercase with the accent: **ΑΥΡΙΟ** 'tomorrow' (stress on the first syllable)
items.why: In αυ, ευ, ου the accent is written on the second letter.

items.prompt: Write in lowercase with the accent: **ΟΙΚΟΓΕΝΕΙΑ** 'family' (stress on -γε-)
items.why: The final -ια is one syllable [ja], so -γέ- is the third-to-last.

items.prompt: Write in lowercase with the accent: **ΠΟΤΕ** 'never'
items.why: ποτέ 'never' is stressed on the end; πότε 'when?' on the start.

items.prompt: Write in lowercase with the accent: **ΠΟΥ** 'where?'
items.why: Monosyllables take no accent, except to tell words apart: question πού vs relative που.

items.prompt: Add **μου**: το τηλέφωνο 'my phone'
items.why: τηλέφωνο is stressed on the third-to-last syllable, so it gains a second accent before μου.

items.prompt: Genitive plural of **άνθρωπος**: των ___
items.why: The long ending -ων pulls the stress to the second-to-last syllable.

items.prompt: Write in lowercase with the accent: **ΕΥΡΩ** 'euro' (stress on the last syllable)
items.why: Final stressed ω takes the accent: ευρώ.
